clue.text: Tips from someone with doubt about traitor leading to seizure

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters of the next word are kept
the doubt is said to be carrying something with it, wrapped around the other piece

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
a doubt is a question raised
a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: Hints from a sceptic about a turncoat end in the traitor's arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is not a signal here: the doubt simply wraps round the traitor, and 'Tips' means the two ends of the word, not advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequestration is the legal confiscation of property, a formal taking of goods into custody.

clue.text: Saint put on garment in flashing light

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for saint
a robe is a long loose garment

explanation.surface: A saint dresses in a robe while lit by a flashing lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the saint is placed on top of the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a lamp producing rapid regular bursts, as used at discos and in photography.

clue.text: Lawman initially trapped by criminal can quote famous Bond movie

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter only of the word it follows
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters that follow are bent out of order
something trapped is held inside the other, so one piece goes within

blocks.note: first letter of the word
three words as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawman is caught by a crook who can quote a well-known 007 film.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'can quote famous' surround the L; 'famous' looks like it describes the film but belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Quantum of Solace is the 2008 James Bond film starring Daniel Craig, the twenty-second in the series.

clue.text: Spontaneously pace about after European vote

indicators.note: after sends the pace-and-about pair second, behind the European vote that ends the clue

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper
tempo is the pace of music
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Someone paces about on impulse after casting a European ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross on a ballot paper is the usual crossword way to show a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore describes speaking or performing without preparation, on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Claw used in brutal onslaught

indicators.note: the letters are put to use inside the following words, lying across their join

blocks.note: found straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A claw is employed in a savage attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Put together article on predicament, upset and drained

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: the indefinite article
to be in a mess is to be in a predicament
bled means drained of blood or fluid

explanation.surface: A writer drafts an article about a crisis, leaving them shaken and exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is the grammar word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembled means constructed by fitting parts together, as with flat-pack furniture.

clue.text: River popular before twilight, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: something in is fashionable
dusk is the evening twilight

explanation.surface: A river grows popular as evening approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river of South Asia flowing through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Roughly right on this name for county

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so the letters that follow come out in a loose, rearranged order

blocks.note: four words as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gives an approximately correct name for an English shire.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottinghamshire is a county in the East Midlands of England, home of Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Risk in hospital restricted by nurse

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as on road signs
to nurse a patient is to treat them

explanation.surface: A hospital patient is at risk, confined by a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' looks like a noun, but it is the verb 'to treat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a danger or menace, something that puts safety at risk.

clue.text: Revolutionary ruler retaining old cook

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the ruler is read backwards
retaining means holding onto, so the ruler keeps the other piece inside

blocks.note: a tsar was the Russian emperor
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader keeps on an elderly chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a description of the ruler's politics; a tsar was the very ruler revolutionaries toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook food by dry heat in an oven or over a fire.

clue.text: Survive scrap that's desperate

blocks.note: to last is to endure or keep going
to ditch something is to discard it

explanation.surface: Coming through a desperate fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight but is the verb meaning to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt made when all else has failed.

clue.text: Roofing material fellows attached to part for all to see

blocks.note: a bit is a part of something
the film certificate U, universal, means suitable for all audiences
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Workmen fix roofing on a section of a building in full public view.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification for universal viewing, suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitumen is a tarry substance used for waterproofing roofs and surfacing roads.

clue.text: Torpedo for instance from ship, one in distance

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces within the word for a distance

blocks.note: SS stands for steamship
Roman numeral one
a mile is a unit of distance

explanation.surface: A torpedo is fired from a ship at something some way off.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater weapon, one example of a guided projectile.

clue.text: Memorable time in base

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word for base

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
base means low and wicked

explanation.surface: An unforgettable spell spent at headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a military camp but is the adjective meaning morally low.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immortal is never forgotten, its fame enduring through the ages.

clue.text: Lifted prize, prize of highest quality

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means raised up, so both words are read bottom to top

blocks.note: a pot is a prize cup, or the money to be won
a prize is a reward

explanation.surface: A trophy is hoisted, and it is a first-rate one.
explanation.walkthrough: Both prizes are raised, so both read upwards. 'Lifted' also suggests stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an informal idiom for first-class or upper-class, the very best.

clue.text: Appeal following search for figure

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the appeal is placed after the search

blocks.note: to dig is to search, as on an excavation
it means sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A petition comes after a hunt for a missing figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the appeal after the search. IT for sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is any numeral from zero to nine, a single figure.

clue.text: Terribly tired, one's leaving

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters come out in a muddled order

blocks.note: the words as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Utterly exhausted, someone is heading off.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is the act of abandoning a post or person, a form of departing.

clue.text: Upset about loud firearm

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: to rile is to annoy
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Someone is disturbed by a noisy gun.
explanation.walkthrough: F is forte, the musical direction for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun with a spirally grooved bore, fired from the shoulder.

clue.text: Stand up to run over development of sites

indicators.note: development means growth and change, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

blocks.note: cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Locals oppose a new housing development planned on local plots.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the run above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to withstand or oppose, much as one stands up to a bully.

clue.text: Editor revised tales after quiet support

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
standard abbreviation
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor reworks stories once given some quiet backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The editor and the reworked tales come after the quiet P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a statue or column stands, a physical support.

clue.text: Insult lacking in substance

blocks.note: first meaning: a snub or affront
second meaning: flimsy, slender or trivial

explanation.walkthrough: One word works as a noun for a snub and as an adjective for something insubstantial.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a deliberate snub, and a slight argument or figure is thin and unimpressive.

clue.text: Small jumper for customer in store?

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as on clothing labels
a hopper is something that hops, such as a grasshopper

explanation.surface: A little sweater for a customer in a clothes shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, which suits a store, but here it is something that hops.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper is a person buying goods; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Guide holy group

blocks.note: pi is informal for pious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Someone leads a religious party.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for holy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to steer or lead the way, as a harbour pilot steers ships.

clue.text: Friend keeping positive about examination

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the friend wraps around the other piece
about here means turned round, so the word for positive reads backwards

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A friend remains upbeat about an upcoming exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or inspection of a document.

clue.text: Gold turning up under stuff in Italian city

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means flipping upward, so the symbol is read bottom to top
in a down entry under places one piece below the other, so the gold comes second

blocks.note: to pad is to stuff or fill out
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Gold turns up beneath the goods in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' puts the reversed gold below the stuff in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Padua is a city in the Veneto region of northern Italy, famous for its university.

clue.text: Accepted second wife, lawful

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
something lawful is allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A man took a second wife, all legal and above board.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story is to believe it or take it without protest.

clue.text: Some artistic ingenuity needed for cake decoration?

indicators.note: some means a portion, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: found straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Decorating a cake calls for a little creative flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on cakes; the question mark marks it as one example of decoration.

clue.text: Go into main tent prepared for show

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or arranged, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: to enter is to go into
two words as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Step into the big top, all set for the circus performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainment is a performance or spectacle staged to amuse an audience.
